_: The five findings of the lapis (Monitoring) hero, in the exact keys of findings-screening.json. Provenance: every figure in a/b/cote is a cell of ~/Documents/cascade-monitoring/releve-public.json at seal `sceau`; the builder refuses to build if the record on disk no longer matches. Each figure keeps its cell address in `source` ({table, palier, seuil, mesure} or {table, compte}); the optional `champ` names which field of the Rate is displayed when it is not `taux` (finding 03 displays lower bounds: champ = 'bas'). Builders may ignore `source`; reviewers and guards re-derive every number from it. The tool's rule behind finding 03 is the same as the whole suite: Wilson lower bound of recall at or above 0.90, then the fewest false alerts. Twin attributions in the phrases are measured, not assumed: at 0.50 the seven false alerts of `amount` are all one-off purchases, and `velocity` trips on payroll, seasonal trade and savings transfers. `annotations` are fractions of the delivered close-up of each state (anchor x, anchor y, label x, label y, text): positions and texts were remeasured against the delivered close-ups (rack-01..05, the travellings' arrival frames arbitrated by Arslane): 01 the amount blade pulled out, 02 the counting blade, 03 the brass line over the three left blades, 04 the written and synthetic pair, 05 the whole rack with the eighth, ivory piece pulled. Two labels changed because the framed piece changed what a viewer can count: in 01 the amount blade half-hides its own amber row, so the label no longer counts seven diodes, and in 02 the false alerts read as a grid, not a row. Every label is 60 characters or fewer, per the builder's rule.

findings.titre: The amount scenario alone reaches 95.2% recall at 16.7% false alerts.
findings.phrase: Scoring only the largest amount in the window reaches 95.2% recall on the 42 cases marked suspicious. It alerts on 16.7% of the 42 cases marked benign, each a one-off family purchase the history explains.
findings.leg_a: recall 95.2% for the amount scenario at 0.50, interval 84% to 99%, 42 cases, all suspicious
findings.leg_b: false alerts 16.7% at 0.50, interval 8% to 31%, 42 cases, all benign

findings.titre: The velocity scenario reaches 28.6% recall and alerts on half the benign cases.
findings.phrase: Counting transactions reaches 28.6% recall, since most suspicious cases are not the busiest accounts. The same count alerts on half the 42 cases marked benign: payroll, seasonal trade and monthly savings.
findings.leg_a: recall 28.6% for the velocity scenario at 0.50, interval 17% to 44%, 42 cases, all suspicious
findings.leg_b: false alerts 50% at 0.50, interval 36% to 64%, 42 cases, all benign

findings.titre: No scenario's recall lower bound reaches the 90% floor.
findings.phrase: The tool holds the Wilson lower bound of recall at 90%, then takes the fewest false alerts. On the 42 cases no single scenario reaches that floor: the best lower bound is 84.2% for amount, the next 75% for peer.
findings.leg_a: highest recall lower bound, amount at 0.50: 84.2%, interval 84% to 99%
findings.leg_b: next best lower bound, peer at 0.50: 75%, interval 75% to 95%
annotations: recall floor 90%: no scenario reaches it

findings.titre: The amount scenario scores 100% recall on generated cases against 95.2% on written ones.
findings.phrase: The same cell scores 95.2% recall on 42 cases written and 100% on 126 cases generated. The generated set is easier, so the tool measures it on its own and keeps it out of the headline rate.
findings.leg_a: recall 95.2% for amount at 0.50 on 42 cases written, interval 84% to 99%
findings.leg_b: recall 100% at the same cell on 126 cases generated, interval 97% to 100%

findings.titre: Measure the whole grid on your own alert history.
findings.phrase: Every rate here comes from the public record: 42 cases marked suspicious and 42 cases marked benign, seven per typology, with 126 cases generated of each. Two files from your systems rerun the grid, and the report lands next to your files.
findings.leg_a: 42 cases suspicious and 42 cases benign, written and declared, seven per typology
findings.leg_b: 126 cases of each, generated under a seed and measured apart
